title: A two-scale heartbeat entropy contrast does not improve primary external CHF log loss despite a small ranking gain
abstract: In 33 discovery and 81 external public participant-recordings, adding scale4-minus-scale1 sample entropy beyond selected time-domain HRV and single-scale entropy raised CHF-versus-NSR source-cohort AUC from 0.8038 to 0.8347 but worsened log loss from 0.5086 to 0.5137. Paired fixed-model 95% intervals included zero for both changes. Lower entropy contrast in CHF transferred descriptively. Strict-cleaning sensitivity improved both metrics but changed discovery eligibility and baseline performance. Quality and template-count adjustment did not establish robust incremental benefit. These are separate-source tests on previously used cohorts, not globally untouched confirmation; enrollment overlap cannot be excluded. Author scalar-count checks, raw-block checks, input hashes and clean reruns are supplied. No clinical utility or nonlinear mechanism is established.
